expo.name: E-Raporto
expo.//splash: backgroundColor is the light surface from the app palette, not the brand navy: the slogan ink is rgb(0,48,72), which would be invisible on a dark ground. A dark-mode variant would need a light-ink export of the logo.

infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: E-Raporto e përdor vendndodhjen tuaj për të treguar problemet pranë jush dhe për të vendosur saktë raportin tuaj në hartë.
infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription: E-Raporto e përdor kamerën që ju të fotografoni problemin që po raportoni.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: E-Raporto lejon bashkëngjitjen e një fotoje ekzistuese në raportin tuaj.

android.//predictiveBackGestureEnabled: Explicit even though false is Expo's own default: Android's predictive-back gesture snapshots the screen as the user drags, and a SurfaceView-backed WebView (the map) does not reliably survive being captured mid-gesture — the blank/frozen screen bug this app hit. Expo Router + predictive back has open compatibility issues beyond this app's map (expo/expo#39092). Written here for the day this app leaves Expo Go for a real build, since Expo Go's own shell ignores this setting entirely.
android.//adaptiveIcon: Brand navy, unlike the splash: the icon carries the emblem alone, so there is no dark wordmark to lose against it.

plugins.locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission: E-Raporto e përdor vendndodhjen tuaj vetëm kur po raportoni ose po shikoni hartën.

plugins.photosPermission: E-Raporto lejon bashkëngjitjen e një fotoje në raportin tuaj.
plugins.cameraPermission: E-Raporto e përdor kamerën që ju të fotografoni problemin.

extra.//apiUrl: Override per-machine with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL in .env. Expo Go on a phone cannot reach 'localhost' — use the dev machine's LAN IP.
extra.//maps: Maps are Leaflet in a WebView (see src/components/LeafletMap.tsx), not react-native-maps: no Google Maps API key, no native module, identical behaviour in Expo Go and in a build.
extra.//eas: Required for real push notifications to work in any build (dev build, TestFlight, or the store). Run `eas init` once from this directory — it adds an `eas.projectId` key here itself, pointing at the project on your Expo account. Until that has been done, the key stays absent and push registration silently no-ops; everything else in the app is unaffected. (Deliberately not present as a null placeholder: Expo Go serves a literal `null` back to the client as an empty object, not as JS null/undefined — a real, if surprising, quirk of how it composes the served manifest — so a placeholder here would actively break the falsy-check in useNotifications.ts rather than just doing nothing.)
